title: Thinking About Moving to La Cañada? It’s District, District, District
author: lacanada.us editorial staff
image_alt: La Cañada Unified School District campus life
excerpt: In La Cañada Flintridge, the modern real-estate saying is district, district, district. LCUSD ranks at or near the top of California unified districts on CAASPP, and that is a big reason families pay a premium to live here.
body_markdown:
There’s an old real-estate saying: **location, location, location.**

In La Cañada Flintridge, you could make a strong case that the modern version is **district, district, district.**

If you’re considering moving to La Cañada, the public school district is one of the biggest reasons families are willing to pay a premium to live here. La Cañada Unified School District (LCUSD) is small, academically intense, well-supported by the community, and currently performing at or near the top of California’s public-school system. Unlike a lot of “best schools” claims you see on real-estate listings, this one is backed up by state testing data.

## Start With the Numbers

According to California’s official 2024–25 CAASPP results:

| Subject               | LCUSD students meeting or exceeding standard | Statewide rank among unified districts |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------: | -------------------------------------: |
| English Language Arts |                                      **89%** |                                 **#1** |
| Mathematics           |                                      **84%** |                                 **#2** |
| Science               |                                      **75%** |                                 **#1** |

In English, 61% of LCUSD students exceeded the standard and another 28% met it. In math, 63% exceeded and 21% met it.

La Cañada ranked first in California in English, first in science, and second in math among unified school districts.

## How Does La Cañada Compare With the Rest of Los Angeles?

Los Angeles County has a wide range of public-school options, from LAUSD to smaller districts such as Arcadia, South Pasadena, San Marino, Manhattan Beach, and Palos Verdes. LCUSD ranks #1 statewide among unified districts in English Language Arts and science, so it also sits at the top of Los Angeles County unified districts in those subjects. Its #2 statewide mathematics ranking puts it one step from the top there as well.

## California Distinguished Schools

In 2023, all three La Cañada Unified elementary schools were named California Distinguished Schools:

- La Cañada Elementary
- Palm Crest Elementary
- Paradise Canyon Elementary

The designation is awarded to individual schools, and California rotates recognition cycles between elementary and secondary schools. It would be inaccurate to say LCUSD itself is a “Distinguished School district.” Having all three elementary schools recognized in the same cycle shows consistency across the system.

## Don't Live in La Cañada? There May Still Be a Path In

LCUSD operates a non-resident permit program that includes an employment-based option commonly associated with California’s Allen Bill provisions. Under the district’s current guidelines, a parent or legal guardian may be eligible to apply if they are physically employed within LCUSD boundaries:

- 32 or more hours per week for the district’s full-time category
- 16 or more hours per week for its part-time category

Applicants generally need an employer letter, a recent pay stub, and student academic records. This is particularly relevant for families connected with NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory. JPL employees have historically used employment-based permits to enroll children in LCUSD, and the district has conducted permit outreach specifically for JPL employees.

A permit is not guaranteed. Residents receive priority, and non-resident students are admitted only when the district determines space is available. LCUSD uses a priority and lottery system. The district also offers other permit categories, including provisions involving district employees, siblings of existing permit students, and certain legacy circumstances.

If you think you may qualify, start with the Non-Resident Permit Applications section of the official LCUSD website. The rules and annual application dates can change, so treat any summary, including this one, as an introduction rather than the final word.

## One Reason the Schools Stay Strong: The Community Helps Pay for Them

The La Cañada Flintridge Educational Foundation (LCFEF) is a major private funding source for the district. Foundation funding helps support smaller class sizes, counselors, technology, music and arts, instructional programs, and teacher staffing and salaries.

LCFEF reported raising about $2.7 million for LCUSD in 2024–25, and the Foundation says its 2025–26 campaign will provide approximately $2.2 million for the 2026–27 school year. For 2026–27, LCFEF is requesting a contribution of $3,500 per family. It is voluntary. Not every household can or should feel obligated to give that amount, but if you move here and can comfortably afford the requested contribution, it is worth considering giving the full amount. One of the reasons the schools can provide programs beyond basic state funding is that local families consistently support them.

## What This Means If You're Considering a Move

No school district is perfect, and test scores alone should never determine whether a community is right for your family. But if public education is a major factor in your move, La Cañada deserves serious consideration.

The numbers are unusually strong:

- 89% of LCUSD students meet or exceed the ELA standard
- 84% meet or exceed the mathematics standard
- 75% meet or exceed the science standard
- #1 among California unified districts in English
- #1 in science
- #2 in mathematics
- All three elementary schools were named California Distinguished Schools in 2023

Add in a small district, substantial community financial support, and a permit program that can create opportunities for some families working locally, and you begin to understand why the school district plays such an outsized role in La Cañada real estate.

In La Cañada, it may still be location, location, location. But for families with children, it’s district, district, district.

*(Curious about who's #1 in math? Here's your clue: the district shares its name with a nearby city whose name is almost identical to that of one of Europe's tiniest countries.)*
